subtopics.title: From Final Accounts to Formal Statement

questions.question: The Statement of Comprehensive Income is built exclusively from:
options: NOMINAL accounts — the incomes and expenses measuring the year's flows

questions.question: The test for sorting any account between the two statements is:
options: Is the amount large or small?
Does it measure the year's FLOW, or the year-end's HOLDING?
Is it a debit or a credit?

questions.question: The statement re-dresses which ledger accounts for the public?
options: The Trading and Profit and Loss accounts — same figures, readable report

questions.question: "FOR the year ended" versus "AT 28 February" marks the difference between:
options: A PERIOD of accumulated flows and a MOMENT'S photographed position

questions.question: The statement's opening lines run:
options: Sales (less debtors allowances), cost of sales in brackets, GROSS PROFIT

questions.question: Gross operating income of R26 000 is:
options: Gross profit R20 000 plus other operating income R6 000

questions.question: Operating profit of R9 100 equals:
options: Gross operating income R26 000 minus operating expenses R16 900

questions.question: The fixed order of the three layers is:
options: Trading, then operating, then financing — each with its own ruled subtotal

questions.question: The Telephone line with workings reads:
options: R1 200 (1 100 + 100) — the paid months plus February still owing

questions.question: Rent Income appears as:
options: R6 000 (5 500 + 500) — the year earned twelve months

questions.question: Interest on the loan belongs:
options: In the financing tail BELOW operating profit — operating profit must measure operations alone

questions.question: Workings are shown in brackets beside each line so that:
options: The auditor can erase them later
The marker can award the ROUTE even where a slip spoils the destination

questions.question: The three layers isolate three diagnoses:
Gross profit of R20 000 on sales of R100 000 tells the owner:
options: The shop kept R20 000 in the bank
Every hundred rand of sales carried twenty rand of margin — the pricing policy delivered

questions.question: The bank compares operating profit R9 100 with interest expense R1 200 to judge:
options: Whether the operations can carry the borrowing — here covering it more than seven times over

questions.question: A mixed-up statement "answers none of the questions" because:
options: Each layer answers a DIFFERENT question, and mixing the layers destroys all three answers

subtopics.title: The Year's Story on One Page

questions.question: The story's fixed plot runs:
options: Sold, cost, first breath (trading profit); other earnings and running costs, second breath (operating profit); borrowing costs, final line (net profit)
Net profit first, then the details

questions.question: "Journey pages and photo pages never mix their contents" means:
options: Statements are drawn in separate months
Flows (the year's earning) and positions (the midnight holding) belong to different statements
Photographs may not appear in reports
The two statements use different currencies

questions.question: The one page exists because:
options: The ledger must be destroyed at year end
One page is cheaper to print
A reader needs the year told in an order anyone can follow — the pile cannot be handed over

questions.question: The top floor's only residents are:
options: What customers paid and what the goods had cost — the trading question

questions.question: The middle floor's question is:
options: Is the SHOP AS A MACHINE healthy — what survives after every cost of keeping doors open?
How much did the owner draw?

questions.question: Trading profit fine, operating profit thin points to:
options: A COST problem — the running floor is leaking

questions.question: The three-floor format beats a one-room statement because:
options: When something goes wrong, the floors tell you WHERE the leak is

questions.question: The loan's interest lands:
options: On the ground floor with the borrowing — the price of money, never a running cost

questions.question: "An unexplained figure earns only itself; an explained one earns its journey" argues for:
options: Writing the bracket working — (1 100 + 100) — beside every adjusted line
Hiding the workings from the marker

questions.question: Depreciation of R1 800 sits on the statement as:
options: A running cost like any other — the year used a year of the machine

questions.question: The whole point of the page, honestly stated:
options: Months of careful work so that ONE page can be TRUSTED by any reader
